Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occrured while the other vehicle was changing lanes. The mechanism
described, a forceful bracing of the outstretched hand against the steering wheel and door frame, is consistent with the wrist
fracture subsequently identified. Radiographs and the physical examination findings together clearly confirm the fracture, with
localized swelling, tenderness over the distal radius, and restricted range of motion at the time of initial evaluation. There is no
record of prior injury or treatment to this body region. Care was delivered over twelve visits and followed a typical course:
immobilization, supervised progression of range-of-motion exercises, and follow-up imaging to confirm healing alignment. Visit
frequency tapered as pain and function improved, and the patient is now discharged to independent home exercise. Two similar
billing entries recorded on the same date of service are currently under review for accuracy.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
